title: Tautology and Contradiction
body:
Three classifications of a single formula, read off the final column of its
[[Truth Table]].

```
tautology    true in every row        P ∨ ¬P
contradiction  false in every row     P ∧ ¬P
contingent   true in some, false in others    P ∧ Q
```

A tautology carries no information about the world, since it is true whatever the facts are,
and that is exactly what makes it useful in logic: a tautology can be added to any argument
without risk. A contradiction entails everything, because there is no row where its premises
are true, so an argument with contradictory premises is valid regardless of its conclusion.

The connection to arguments is direct. An argument is valid exactly when the conditional whose
antecedent is the conjunction of the premises and whose consequent is the conclusion is a
tautology, which is why one test covers both questions.
